tagline: Across the Green River into the Everly family's Muhlenberg County.
intro: From the Union County line, KY 56 runs east through Webster County to Sebree, then on into McLean County and down KY 136 to Calhoun on the Green River. KY 81 heads south through Sacramento into Muhlenberg County, and US 431 carries the trail through Central City before it loops west and back east on US 62 to the Ohio County line.

Ike Everly went into the coal mines at 14, and his father encouraged him to follow his love of music. His son Don was born in 1937 at Brownie, since folded into Central City. In 1988 the city started an Everly Brothers Homecoming on Labor Day weekend, and the weekend goes on as a car show.

moments.title: Calhoun
moments.text: Henry Rhoads laid out the town in the 1780s by the Long Falls of the Green River, and the Army Corps of Engineers keeps Lock and Dam No. 2 at Calhoun now.

moments.title: Sacramento
moments.text: Named, local tradition says, by a man just home from the California Gold Rush, the town saw Forrest's First Fight in December 1861 and still reenacts it every year.

moments.title: Drakesboro
moments.text: The Four Legends Fountain honors four pioneers of thumb-picked guitar with close ties to Muhlenberg County, Kennedy Jones, Ike Everly, Mose Rager and Merle Travis.
